style.vernacular: Middle Belt savanna town and Nasarawa State capital. Ordinary buildings are single-storey cement-block houses and shops in painted render (cream, light green, ochre) with rust-red or green corrugated metal roofs; older Hausa/Lafia-emirate compounds use mud-render with arched doorways; newer state and university buildings are 2-4 storey concrete blocks in white or pale cream. Laterite roads, shea, neem and mango trees.
style.ornament: Hausa-emirate arched doorways and relief on palace gates; flat-fronted rendered shops with hand-painted signs; white-painted state buildings with flagpoles; mosque domes and short minarets on the 1971 state mosque.
